tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Show Cause Notice (SCN) dated 08-02-2012 for ₹12.94 million was issued by Commissioner of Central Excise Chandigarh alleging availment of ineligible CENVAT Credit. The Company filed a Writ Petition for quashing of SCN. Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana allowed Writ Petition vide Order dated 26-11-2019 and quashed the SCN. Union of India represented through Commissioner of Central GST, Delhi East preferred Special Leave Petition (SLP) before Hon’ble Supreme Court of India on 22-12-2020 against the High Court’s Order.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Union of India represented through Commissioner of Central GST, Delhi East
tax_litigation.status: The matter is pending before Supreme Court. No change during the quarter.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Income tax demand of ₹162.22 million in respect to Assessment Year 2005-06 was raised by the Income Tax Department based on certain grounds related to purchases made by the Company from an overseas vendor. The matter was decided in favour of the Company and the addition of income was deleted by Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) ("CIT (Appeals)"). However, the Income Tax Department has filed an appeal before Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) against the order of CIT (Appeals) which is pending at present.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle-05, New Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The appeal before ITAT is pending at present. No change during the quarter.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Demand Order dated 29-01-2015 was issued by the Commissioner of Central Excise, Delhi raising demand of ₹62.50 million with penalty and interest of ₹8.10 million on account of non-payment of service tax u/s 68 on gross value of taxable services. The Company filed an appeal before Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, Delhi (“CESTAT”) against the said demand order which was allowed by CESTAT. However, Commissioner of Central GST, New Delhi preferred an appeal before the Delhi High Court (“DHC”) on 30-09-2020 which was rejected vide its order dated 10-09-2024. The said Commissioner then filed a Review Petition on 15-11-2024 before DHC against its order.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Commissioner of Central GST, New Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The matter is pending before Delhi High Court. No change during the quarter.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: A search operation was conducted by the Income Tax Department in the premises of the Company in January 2012 and hence the Company had re-filed the income tax returns for the Assessment Year 2006-07 to 2012-13. During the year ended March 31, 2015, the Income Tax Department completed the assessment of the said years, disallowed certain expenses on various grounds including purchases made from overseas party, FCCB raised, payment to overseas party and freebies given to doctors and issued demand of ₹3,294.90 million (including interest). The Company preferred appeals before the CIT (Appeals) against the orders of the Income Tax Department. The appeals were decided in favour of the Company and the demand was cancelled. However, CIT (Appeals) has made certain disallowances with respect to Assessment Year 2010-11 and 2011-12 against which the Company has filed appeals before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT). The Income Tax Department has also filed appeals before ITAT against the orders of CIT (Appeals).
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle-05, New Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The appeals before ITAT are pending at present. No change during the quarter.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Demand of ₹33.69 million was raised by Income tax department vide its order dated 30-04-2021 on account of disallowance made by transfer pricing officer on purchases from / payment of expenses to, related parties in Assessment Year 2016-17. tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle-05, New Delhi

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Earlier, a demand of ₹57.45 million towards balance amount of Goods and Service Tax ("GST") (including interest & penalty thereon) on assignment of leasehold rights in land and building by the Company in Navi Mumbai, was raised by the Office of the Assistant Commissioner of State Tax. tax_litigation.status: PBPL has filed appeal before the GST Appellate Tribunal on 21-07-2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Demand of ₹6.36 million was raised by Income Tax department vide its order dated 22-03-2025 on account of disallowance of certain expenditure for the Asesstment Year 2023-24. The Company filed an appeal with CIT(A) against such Order. CIT(A) dismissed the appeal.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Office of Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The Company filed an appeal to ITAT against such order on 13-04-2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Demand Order of ₹70.34 million was received from the Assistant Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai towards balance amount of Goods and Service Tax ("GST") (including interest & penalty thereon) on assignment of leasehold rights in land and building by the Company in Navi Mumbai. The Company filed writ petition before the Hon’ble Bombay High Court, challenging the said Order on 04-09-2025. The Hon'ble High Court issued an interim order dated 25-02-2026 pursuant to which the authority has been directed that pending the hearing and final disposal of the petition, no recovery under the impugned orders shall be adopted against the Company.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Office of the Assistant Commissioner of State Tax, GST Bhawan, Mazgaon, Mumbai, Maharashtra
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed a refund application on 03-04-2026 before Maharashtra GST Authorities for seeking refund of tax & interest paid under protest amounting to ₹31.4 million. tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Show cause notice (SCN) was issued under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (CGST Act) regarding alleged non-payment of GST of ₹114.40 million on providing Corporate Guarantee amounting to ₹8,640 million to Debenture Trustee viz. Vistra ITCL (India) Limited in relation to transfer of pharmaceutical formulations business to the Company’s wholly owned subsidiary viz. Panacea Biotec Pharma Limited, for 1,074 days from 06-04-2019 to 15-03-2022. The Company filed writ petition before the Hon’ble Punjab & Haryana High Court on 24-11-2025, challenging the said Order. The Hon'ble High Court passed an interim stay order stating inter-alia that no coercive action be taken against the Company in case of final assessment order is passed or a demand is raised. In the meantime, Joint Commissioner, CGST Sub-Commissionerate Mohali, Chandigarh issued a Demand Order dated 30-03-2026 raising demand aggregating to ~₹228.80 million (towards alleged non-payment of GST of ~₹114.40 million and penalty of ~₹114.40 million).
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Office of the Commissioner, Central GST (Audit) Commissionerate, Punjab
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal before Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Cour against the order on 25.06.2026. The matter is pending before the Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Demand aggregating to ₹93.88 million was raised by Income Tax department vide its three Demand Orders dated 24-12-2025, imposing penalty on account of alleged under reporting of income. tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, New Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal with ITAT on 11.05.2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company filed rebate claims of Excise Duty before the Assistant Commsioner of Central Excise which was partly allowed in the form of CENVAT Credit amounting to ₹3.46 million instead of repayment in cash. PBL filed an appeal before Commissioner (Appeals) wherein repayment of claims in cash was allowed and the same was credited into Company's Account. However, Department filed revision application with Joint Secretary, Government of India against the said order which was accepted in favour of Department. Then, the Company filed writ petition before the Delhi High Court against such decision and the same was admitted.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Central Excise, New Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The matter is pending before the Delhi High Court. No change during the quarter.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Show Cause Notice (SCN) dated 08-02-2012 for ₹12.94 million was issued by Commissioner of Central Excise Chandigarh alleging availment of ineligible CENVAT Credit. The Company filed a Writ Petition for quashing of SCN. Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana allowed Writ Petition vide Order dated 26-11-2019 and quashed the SCN. Union of India represented through Commissioner of Central GST, Delhi East preferred Special Leave Petition (SLP) before Hon’ble Supreme Court of India on 22-12-2020 against the High Court’s Order. The Company has requested the concerned Deputy Commissioner, CGST (Derabassi) to file suitable application to withdraw the SLP as per the instructions issued by the CBIC under Section 35R of the Central Excise Act 1944, prohibiting filing of appeals etc. by the Department to higher Authorities when the amount of taxes involved is less than the prescribed limits.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Union of India represented through Commissioner of Central GST, Delhi East
tax_litigation.status: The matter is pending before Hon'ble Supreme Court. No change during the quarter.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Demand Order of ₹62.50 million with penalty and interest of ₹8.10 million was issued by the Commissioner of Central Excise, Delhi on account of non-payment of service tax u/s 68 on gross value of taxable services. However, Commissioner of Central GST, New Delhi preferred an appeal before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court (“DHC”) on 30-09-2020 which was rejected vide its order dated 10-09-2024. Thereafter, the said Commissioner then filed a Review Petition on 15-11-2024 before DHC against order dated 10-09-2024.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Commissioner of Central GST, New Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The matter is pending before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court. No change during the quarter.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Demand of ₹33.69 million was raised by Income tax department vide its order dated 30-04-2021 on account of disallowance made by transfer pricing officer on purchases from / payment of expenses to, related parties in Assessment Year 2016-17. tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle-05, New Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The appeal before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court is pending at present. No change during the quarter.

timeline.summary: On April 30, 2026, Panacea Biotec announced that the ITAT allowed its appeal, cancelling a ₹9.16 Cr tax demand for AY 2020-21.
On April 30, 2026, Panacea Biotec reported a fire incident due to a short circuit at its subsidiary's Baddi oncology facility, causing a 5-7 day disruption.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹166.75 Cr (+25.8% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹0.52 Cr (against a loss of ₹1.89 Cr a year earlier).
On June 5, 2026, promoter Rajesh Jain (HUF) disclosed a proposed nil-price gift acquisition of 2,00,000 Panacea Biotec shares (0.09%) from Dr. Rajesh Jain, on or after June 12, 2026.
On June 8, 2026, Panacea Biotec announced its participation as a key partner in the EU-funded DENSTAR project to advance licensure of its DengiAll® vaccine in sub-Saharan Africa.
